transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we've got 45 minutes, goal is to lock the canary date and final cutover/runbook items. quick roll call?
[00:08] Marta Lopez: Marta here, hey.
[00:10] Ben Carter: Ben present.
[00:12] Sasha Nguyen: Sasha, product.
[00:14] Ravi Patel: Ravi from security.
[00:16] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood SE.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Jordan in CSM.
[00:22] Alex: Cool. quick recap from last week: we've completed the load test baseline, average p95 latency at our dev endpoints was ~220ms for 512 tokens, cost per 1k tokens improved with the quantized profile. any clarifications before we jump into canary plan?
[00:40] Marta: That matches our numbers, though we saw a few spikes during concurrency tests where p99 hit 1.2s for a short burst. not sure if that was the model or network.
[00:49] Priya: yep we saw that in the logs; those aligned with KV cache cold-starts when multiple prefixes hit new contexts. we suggested small warmup traffic during the canary to populate cache.
[01:02] Ben: on infra side we need to confirm that dedicated nodes have the right autoscaling policy; we don't want to hit burst throttles during the canary.
[01:10] Alex: good call. Ben, can you confirm what autoscale thresholds you want?
[01:14] Ben: thinking: scale up at 60% GPU util, scale down at 30, with a burst buffer of 2 extra instances for 10 minutes. that should handle the ramp.
[01:24] Priya: perfect, we'll mirror that in the Redwood Dedicated config and ensure burst capacity mapping is set.
[01:30] Sasha: timeline - we want to cut over mid next week if all checks pass, product is ready for limited customer testing.
[01:36] Alex: propose Wed 2026-04-29 10am PT for canary. plan: 10:00 start with 5% traffic, 10:30 move to 25% if metrics stable, 11:00 full 100% for the pilot group, and rollback window until 12:00. thoughts?
[01:53] Marta: sounds reasonable, what's the acceptance criteria?
[01:57] Alex: decision criteria: p95 < 400ms, error rate < 0.5%, model quality regression within acceptable delta (we'll use the agreed prompt set), and no security incidents. we should also watch costs; if token cost per req increases beyond 20% of baseline we pause.
[02:20] Marta: can we automate the canary checks? we want thresholds to be enforced rather than manual.
[02:25] Priya: absolutely. Redwood Console supports canary policies - we can set automated gates that will halt rollout on metric breaches. i'll include the exact policy JSON in the runbook, but for this call we'll agree thresholds.
[02:38] Ravi: from security: confirm audit logs and KMS access are enabled for the dedicated cluster. we need to see key rotation policy and that logs are shipped to our SIEM.
[02:47] Ben: we have KMS in place but i need to confirm cross-account key access to Redwood's service account. i'll validate and reply by monday.
[02:55] Alex: ok add that to action items.
[02:58] Priya: about monitoring - we'll provide dashboards for token-level cost, latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, and model quality diffs compared to baseline. do you have an existing pager on-call?
[03:10] Sasha: product has on-call engineers, but we'll need to make sure paging rules are in place for the pilot window.
[03:16] Jordan: Redwood can hook into your OpsSlack channel, or we can push alerts to PagerDuty - which do you prefer?
[03:22] Ben: PagerDuty is preferred. we'll share the integration key.
[03:26] Priya: great, include that in the runbook.
[03:30] Alex: rollback strategy - immediate rollback to previous model endpoint if error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes, or p95 > 800ms sustained for 10 minutes, or critical security alert. rollback steps will be in runbook: DNS switchback + traffic router revert and quick smoke tests.
[03:49] Marta: and who owns the rollback?
[03:52] Ben: platform owns the actual network cut, product signs off on quality, and Redwood SE initiates model rollback. we'll document exact handoff times.
[04:02] Priya: i'll put explicit owner lines in the runbook.
[04:06] Alex: communication plan - pre-cutover slack channel, a short pre-check at T-minus 30, then status updates at each phase. we'll do a post-mortem within 24 hours.
[04:17] Sasha: agree. also need A/B toggles for a segment of users to compare responses. can we run A/B during the canary?
[04:24] Priya: yes we can do a canary with A/B traffic splitting. recommended to keep A/B for 25% of canary traffic and collect quality signals.
[04:33] Marta: what about legal / terms for pilot? any data residency or retention concerns?
[04:37] Ravi: from security, ensure logs for pilot are retained 90 days and encryption keys remain customer-managed. we also need a signed DPA addendum - legal will follow up.
[04:48] Alex: we'll surface the DPA to legal. noted.
[04:50] Ben: one more infra item - cold start: Priya you mentioned warmup traffic. we'll need a script that fires prefix warmups 5 minutes before canary. can you provide that?
[04:58] Priya: yes, i'll post the warmup script and parameterized load tool; it'll be part of the test harness.
[05:05] Marta: for acceptance metrics, i'll share the prompt set and expected outputs by monday - we need reproducible evals.
[05:12] Priya: great, we'll run automatic evals and attach the quality diffs to the dashboard.
[05:17] Alex: pricing/cost question - Sasha asked internally about cost per 1k tokens. during pilot we'll track and compare to baseline, and if it deviates >20% we'll pause. Sasha anything to add?
[05:27] Sasha: just that finance needs a quick estimate for pilot run; Alex can you send an expected cost for two weeks of pilot traffic?
[05:33] Alex: yes i'll send a short estimate after the call.
[05:36] Jordan: recap next steps - canary date 2026-04-29, runbook and monitoring links by 2026-04-24, canary load test plan by 2026-04-24, infra confirmations by 2026-04-26.
[05:48] Marta: ok good. any blockers?
[05:50] Ben: none besides VPC/KMS check which i'm on.
[05:53] Ravi: security will do DPA and KMS verification.
[05:56] Alex: perfect. final question - do you want Redwood to run the canary or do you prefer to trigger it from your side?
[06:02] Ben: prefer Redwood triggers with our platform confirmation, that way rollback tooling stays consistent.
[06:08] Priya: no problem, we'll coordinate with Ben for the trigger.
[06:12] Alex: ok i'll send calendar invite for the canary window and include the runbook. any final comments?
[06:18] Sasha: none.
[06:19] Marta: thanks all.
[06:21] Alex: thanks team, talk soon.
[06:25] (meeting ends)
